critical.issue: CROSS-TENANT LEAK (P0 blocker). Tenant A (isis-admin) sees tenant B's appointment tagged 'LEAK-TEST for SAWALI SMART SYSTEMS-Client' and vice-versa. Endpoint at server.py:7768 still calls db.appointments.find({}, ...) without scoping by _is_super_admin/_resolve_visible_client_ids. The fix was applied to /me/notes/* and other collections but NOT to /admin/appointments, /admin/interventions, /admin/documents (interventions & documents happen to be empty in the LEAK dataset so they passed — but the same code pattern find({}) leaks whenever data exists).

Second duplicate of the same recipe produces name '(copie)' again instead of '(copie 2)'. Root cause : routes/production.py:492-497 does find_one({"name": {"$regex": f"^{candidate}$"}}) with candidate='<name> (copie)' — the unescaped parentheses are interpreted as a regex capture group so the query matches 'name copie' but NOT 'name (copie)'. Fix : use re.escape(candidate) around the regex payload, OR do a plain equality query (case-insensitive via collation).

rca of the issue: P0 leak on /admin/appointments — the Iter43-fix24az-l refactor covered all /me/notes/* branches and several other endpoints (via _is_super_admin helper introduced at server.py:659) but missed the three admin_* endpoints declared with the older 'admin bypass = full DB' pattern : admin_appointments (7768), admin_interventions (7816), admin_documents (7911). Interventions & documents happened to have no LEAK data so the test passed by coincidence — the vulnerability is architectural. Duplicate-recipe (copie 2) : Python f-string `f"^{candidate}$"` embeds `Gel Hydro Douceur (copie)` verbatim into the regex, so `(copie)` becomes a regex group; MongoDB regex engine matches `Gel Hydro Douceur copie` (no parens) which never appears in the collection, so the loop exits immediately and idx stays at 2 (never used). Solution : re.escape() the candidate.
